name: Ford - Van Dyke Electric Powertrain Center, Sterling Heights MI

fieldNotes.site: Ford Van Dyke Electric Powertrain Center, 41111 Van Dyke Ave, Sterling Heights (Macomb County) MI - a ~2M sq ft Ford powertrain plant operating since 1968, renamed in 2021 from the Van Dyke Transmission Plant as it shifted to producing electric motors and transaxles for hybrid/EV vehicles (incl. the F-150 Lightning). LOCATION CORRECTION: the roster address (8000 Van Dyke Ave) and geocode (42.3892,-83.0222, RANGE_INTERPOLATED) are WRONG - they point at a residential Detroit neighborhood ~23 km south. Web research (Detroit News, Ford Authority, AmericanAutoWorker, Yelp) confirms the correct address 41111 Van Dyke Ave, Sterling Heights MI 48314, just north of 18 Mile Rd. Corrected center to ~42.5978,-83.0355 - confirmed by satellite as the large multi-roof Ford plant building.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed - Street View (2025-03) on the north road shows a chain-link sliding truck/vehicle gate (closed, with a gate-number sign) across a wide driveway leading down an internal access drive to the west-side material/dock yard. The property is fully encircled by chain-link perimeter fencing. truckGateCount estimated 2 (a separate north employee/vehicle entrance plus the gated truck drive) - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true at medium confidence - a fenced ~2M sq ft active Ford powertrain plant of this scale conventionally operates a staffed gatehouse at the main entry. No booth was positively resolved at the NW truck gate (which appears badge/remote-style); flagged uncertain along with remoteGs.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: True - the NW truck gate opens onto a long, wide internal access drive with ample paved staging room before reaching the dock yard.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: True - the access drive from the NW gate to the west dock yard is long and deep, with room for 3+ trucks to queue.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 10-25 dock doors along the west building face; a dock bank with trailers backed in is visible in Street View and z19 imagery. Exact count obscured by roof angle - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: West-side material/dock yard holds an estimated 10-20 trailers amid a large laydown area of stacked steel racks / returnable containers; banded 10-25. dropYard true.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Marked false (medium confidence) - the main freight operation (docks + drop yard) is concentrated on the west side; no clearly separate second dock cluster confirmed. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail lines run along the west property edge with spurs serving the west material yard - rail-served.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: True - the NW truck gate apron and internal access drive are very wide with substantial unused paved width; physical room exists for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: False - a single large interconnected plant building (multi-roof but one structure) plus a detached SE office; buildingCount 2.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Sterling Heights is a dense Detroit-metro suburb; the plant is surrounded by continuous suburban/industrial development - Urban.
